topology: 1 node x4 H100, NVSHMEM put-ring (kernel-filtered to put_to_next)
golden: committed (verified); NVSHMEM 3.7 device attribution unreliable, see peer_fanout
workload_note: `mpirun -np 4 ... putget 65536 3`. put_to_next issues one peer store per element per iteration, so elems*iters = 196608 stores of 4 B per rank, and — because the ring gives each PE exactly one neighbour — to exactly one peer device. The volume oracle holds; the attribution one does not.

expect_fail_asserts.peer_fanout: NVSHMEM 3.7 heap attribution — one real edge is split across two adjacent phantom devices, so fan-out reads 2 for a one-neighbour ring. Blocked on PLAN-20260803-1448-nvshmem-heap-attribution. This assertion is that plan's acceptance test; do not edit it to match.
expect_fail_asserts.no_local_loads: Same bug: the PE's local read of src[i] is attributed to a phantom device, so it survives the peer-only RemoteFilter and doubles the access count. 07_nvshmem_multinode runs the identical binary with correct attribution and records zero loads.
expect_fail_asserts.owner_in_range: Same bug: mem_dev comes back as 65..69 (job 44113361) and 238..242 (44111484) for a 4-GPU node. The out-of-range value is the most direct evidence of the fault and the earliest thing a fix should make go away.
